newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market slow at $66 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market slow at $66 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Monday were extremely slow going into the New Year's holiday on Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
About 100 select and choice heifers in Kansas sold at $66.00 per cwt, according to USDA and private sources.
The sales were steady with last year's top price. There were no sales reported from Texas panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots, they said.
Fed cattle prices this week were expected to be supported by ideas that several packers were short on slaughter inventories for post-holiday slaughter, the feedlot sources said.

Light support was attributed to strength in CME live cattle futures following Friday's bullishly construed USDA quarterly hog inventory report, which sent pork complex futures limit-up, market sources said.
The report showed four percent fewer hogs as of December 1 than a year ago and showed farmers were not rebuilding herds as expected.
